The paragraph describes a scenario where the retail store 'Best Deals' extended working hours during the holiday season without increasing pay. The employees were already working the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws.

From a legal compliance perspective, requiring employees to work beyond the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws is generally a violation of labor regulations, regardless of whether it is framed as a "one-time exception" or due to high demand. Labor laws typically set strict limits on working hours to protect employee health and safety, and these limits cannot usually be waived by employer discretion or temporary business needs. Additionally, if the extension of hours resulted in overtime work, failure to pay the required overtime rate would constitute a violation of wage and hour laws. Therefore, the actions described likely violate local labor laws concerning maximum working hours and potentially wage regulations.
